case_name: Hari Shankar and another v State of U. P. and another

The Judgment was delivered by: Faizan Uddin, J.

facts: In session trial No. 395/1976, the appellant Hari Shanker was charged and tried under Section 302, IPC, along with respondent Shiam Behari, who was charged and tried under Section 302/34, IPC.

The High Court of Allahabad gave the benefit of doubt to respondent Shiam Behari and acquitted him of the offence he was charged with. However, the appeal of the applicant Hari Shanker was dismissed by the High Court against which he has filed Criminal Appeal No. 30, 1988.
Smt. Sushmila Devi, the wife of deceased Parshadi Lal had/leased her land to respondent Shiam Behari on January 12, 1972 for purposes of manufacture of bricks.
One Rejesh Kumar, brother of son-in-law of Ved Prakash PW 1, resident of the same locality in Budaun had died but the deceased Parshadi Lal could not join the funeral for want of information.
The deceased Parshadi Lal went to the house of Sita Ram, the father of Rajesh Kumar in Mohalla Chaudhary Sarai along with his friend Chandra Pal Varshney, PW 4 for condolence.

At about 1:00 PM, respondent Shiam Behari and the appellant Hari Shanker also reached there at the house of Sita Ram where respondent Shiam Behari raised Bhatta dispute with deceased Parshadi Lal and protested against the notice served on him.

On the same day at about 2:00 PM when Chandra Pal, PW3 of Brahampur, Budaun arrived at the house of Sita Ram, the deceased Parshadi Lal accompanied by Chandra Pal Varshney, PW 4 got up to go back home.
Parshadi Lal kicked his Motor Cycle to start but it could not start. He and Chandra Pal Varshney then pushed the Motor Cycle with a view to start it.

In the meanwhile, the appellant Hari Shanker with a single barrel gun and respondent Shiam Behari came running from behind. Shiam Behari caught hold of the Motor Cycle from behind and commanded the appellant Hari Shanker to fire at Parshadi Lal and kill him.

At this, the appellant Hari Shanker fired a gun shot on the back of Parshadi Lal who fell on the ground and the appellant Hari Shanker and respondent Shiam Behari immediately vanished from the place of occurrence and while going away Hari Shanker threw down the spent cartridge and loaded the gun again.
issues: There is no motive for the crime.
The direct evidence was not liable to be rejected even if there was no motive for the crime.
The ocular testimony of the witnesses as to the occurrence could not be discarded only by reason of the absence of motive, if otherwise the evidence was worthy of reliance.
petitioner_arguments: There is no reliable evidence to show any altercation between the deceased and the acquitted accused/respondent Shiam Behari with regard to the outstanding dues in respect of the Bhatta land.
The allegation of altercation prior to the incident of firing has not been supported by the prosecution witness Chandra Pal, PW 3.
The ocular version of these so-called eye witnesses could not be accepted in sustaining the conviction of the appellant Hari Shanker.
There is no consistency in the medical evidence and the ocular version of PW 1, PW 3 and PW 4.
respondent_arguments: There was heated exchange between respondent Shiam Behari and the deceased with regard to the Bhatta dues against Shiam Behari.
The direct evidence was not liable to be rejected even if there was no motive for the crime.
The ocular testimony of the witnesses as to the occurrence could not be discarded only by reason of the absence of motive, if otherwise the evidence was worthy of reliance.
court_reasoning: It is settled law that if the genesis of the motive of the occurrence was not proved the ocular testimony of the witnesses as to the occurrence could not be discarded only by reason of the absence of motive, if otherwise the evidence was worthy of reliance.
The evidence of' the prosecution witness Chandra Pal, PW 3 goes to show that there is a close relationship between Hari Shanker and respondent Shiam Behari.

Ved Prakash, PW 1 and Chandra Pal Varshney, PW 4 both have categorically stated that there was heated exchange between the respondent Shiam Behari and the deceased Parshadi Lal with regard to the Bhatta dues against Shiam Behari.
holding: The conviction of the appellant Hari Shanker has been upheld by the High Court.
The order of acquittal of Shiam Behari recorded by the High Court has been challenged by Subhash Chand, the son of deceased Parshadi Lal in Criminal Appeal No. 29 of 1988.
